title: Decode Ambassador: model switching, early-accept gating, and staged failsafe
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement an "ambassador" orchestration layer inside the runtime to support speculative decoding across model variants with a gated early-accept mechanism and staged fallback. The goal is to safely route requests to faster, cheaper model variants where the runtime predicts equivalent output quality while ensuring deterministic, auditable fallbacks to conservative models when confidence is low or kernels are incompatible.
acceptance_criteria: Ambassador component routes requests to a candidate fast-path model variant based on per-request routing policy and kernel compatibility checks
Early-accept metric (top-logit-gap based) computed in prefill and exposeable in per-request trace

If early-accept >= threshold, speculative decode commits and response served within target latency SLO; otherwise runtime falls back to conservative model with < 3x latency increase and no quality regression > 1% on regression suites
Circuit-breaker: if candidate-accept rate drops > 15% relative to baseline or model-quality drift detected, ambassador automatically disables speculative routing for that model and triggers alert
End-to-end e2e test with synthetic and sampled production traces demonstrating safe rollback and no customer-facing errors for 2000 simulated QPS
implementation_plan: Phase A (spike, 2w): prototype ambassador control loop + kernel compatibility matrix; measure kernel mismatch penalties on tensor cores vs fp16 paths
Phase B (impl, 3w): integrate early-accept calculator into prefill stage (logit-gap + entropy delta + KV-cache-hit heuristics); wire per-request trace tags
Phase C (canary, 2w): 1% traffic canary with synthetic prompts, enable speculative routing with conservative thresholds; monitor quality/regression dashboards
Phase D (rollout, 1w): progressive ramp with automated rollback on circuit-breaker conditions and postmortem checklist
experiments: early-accept heuristics A/B: top-logit-gap threshold vs entropy-delta threshold; measure false-accept vs missed-opportunity
kernel-aware routing: prefer kernels with affinity score > 0.8; measure token-latency delta and KV-cache invalidation rate
soft-commit window: allow speculative commit after N decode tokens if acceptance confidence stable for M tokens; tune N/M on short vs long context prompts
risks: Silent quality regressions if early-accept signal correlates poorly with human-evaluated quality for certain instruction families
Kernel incompatibilities causing silent decode truncation or OOM when switching between quantized and fp16 variants
Telemetry gaps: missing trace tags will make root-cause of fallbacks slow to determine
Increased operational complexity for Dedicated customers who pin model versions and expect deterministic latency
open_questions: What is the canonical acceptance SLO for decisioning: maximize throughput under <=1% quality regression, or hold quality strictly?
Should the ambassador persist per-customer routing preferences (e.g., prefer cost savings) or be single global policy?
How to make acceptance thresholds explainable in console and auditable for compliance customers?
What safe mapping exists between kernel variants to enable zero-loss fallback for KV cache semantics?
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-02-16: use a composite early-accept score = normalized top-logit-gap * 0.7 + (1 - entropy_norm) * 0.3 as initial heuristic; log both components for tuning
Decision 2026-02-22: implement kernel compatibility matrix that tracks model-arch -> kernel-family compatibility and a per-hostness penalty factor
Trade-off: aggressive thresholds reduce cost but increase fallback churn—we will start conservative and bias toward fallbacks during canary

Fallback policy: immediate synchronous fallback to conservative variant on prefill-detect failure; if failure occurs mid-decode, fall back by aborting speculative stream and re-dispatching full request to conservative path
